text:
paula: Hi team — quick policy check. I'm traveling in Mexico for 3 weeks but have weekly teletherapy sessions with my US-based, in-network therapist. Are those sessions covered while I'm outside the US? Also I paid one session out-of-pocket last week (receipt attached). What do I need to submit for reimbursement if they're out-of-network or not automatically covered?

jordan (Benefits): Short answer: it depends on the carrier and the plan. Some carriers cover telehealth internationally, others require the clinician to be licensed in the country you're physically located in. We can check your specific plan. If you paid OOP, we'll need an invoice, proof of payment, provider NPI (or local license), and a short note describing service dates. DM me the receipt and provider info and we'll open a claim.

paula: Thanks — receipt is a PayPal transaction for $120 on 2026-04-02 and the therapist is licensed in CA (NPI 1234567890). Therapist did a short clinical note for that session.

kevin: If your carrier won't cover while physically abroad, you can still file a reimbursement claim but approval is not guaranteed. Also some carriers allow an exception for continuity of care — worth asking.

benefits-bot: Automated: For telehealth while traveling, carriers vary. To file a reimbursement upload: 1) itemized invoice; 2) proof of payment (bank/PayPal statement); 3) provider credential (NPI or license); 4) clinical note; 5) employee explanation. Typical adjudication 2-6 weeks. For urgent appeals mark subject "URGENT: Telehealth Reimb".

jordan (Benefits): Also note timezone/MA jurisdiction issues — some carriers specifically require the clinician be licensed where the patient is located at the time of service. If that's the case the claim may be paid as an out-of-network benefit if plan allows. We can request an exception for continuity of care; include therapist attestation stating they're providing care remotely while you travel and any emergency plan.

amir: FYI if you want a quick proof of coverage to show the therapist or a clinic, benefits@redwood.com can issue an internal benefit confirmation letter within 1 business day. That letter includes plan start date and policy number but not a guarantee of payment. Helps with direct-bill attempts or to show to the therapist.

paula: Great. If I submit the PayPal screenshot + clinical note + therapist NPI, how long until I get confirmation you filed the claim?

jordan (Benefits): We'll confirm intake within 1-2 business days and then submit to the carrier. Carrier adjudication is typically 2-6 weeks. If you need faster, request "expedited review" in your email and we'll flag it — carriers sometimes expedite for ongoing mental health care.

paula: One more: will a digital ID card help here? Therapist asked for insurer phone and policy code for billing attempts.

benefits-bot: Digital ID cards are issued by the carrier after enrollment confirmation. We can request the insurer phone and plan code in the internal confirmation letter so you can share with the therapist. Some carriers provide a billing phone for international/dynamic telehealth questions.

paula: Thanks everyone — I'll DM the receipt and provider NPI to Jordan and include a short note about continuity of care. Appreciate it. :pray:
